NXP launches a unified robotics platform, starting with drones

The Neural Axis architecture connects sensing, AI and control; service-robot and AMR support is planned for the second half of 2027.

NXP ↗9 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Reducing integration work

NXP announced a robotics platform based on its Neural Axis architecture on November 9. It connects sensing, AI processing, real-time control and communications, with an open SDK and validated interoperable subsystems. The goal is to reduce hardware and software integration work for developers.

Drone hardware comes first

The initial reference design combines a NavQ95 computer using i.MX 95, a Tropic VMU/FMU using i.MX RT1064, a 100Base-T1 sensor node and motor-control electronics. It supports tools including PX4, Zephyr and ROS 2, alongside drivers, middleware and sample applications.

Availability and the roadmap

NXP says basic drone functionality can be brought up in about 30 minutes out of the box. That is not a claim that a fully certified autonomous drone can be built in that time. The SDK and drone reference design are available initially; broader autonomous-system, service-robot and AMR support is planned for the second half of 2027.
